title: How many patterns?

milestone.title: Binary: The Language of the Machine

description:
Each extra bit doubles the number of patterns. Write:

```python
def patterns(bits)        # how many different patterns that many bits can make
def bits_needed(things)   # the fewest bits that give every one of that many things its own pattern
```

`patterns(8)` is 256. `bits_needed(10)` is 4, because 3 bits give only 8 patterns and 4 bits give 16. One thing needs no bits at all: `bits_needed(1)` is 0.

`2 ** n` is 2 to the power `n` in Python. A `while` loop repeats as long as its condition is true:

```python
bits = 0
while patterns(bits) < things:
    bits = bits + 1
```
unitTests:
@test("patterns double with every bit")
def _():
    check_eq(patterns(0), 1)
    check_eq(patterns(1), 2)
    check_eq(patterns(8), 256)
    check_eq(patterns(32), 4294967296)

@test("bits needed")
def _():
    check_eq(bits_needed(1), 0)
    check_eq(bits_needed(2), 1)
    check_eq(bits_needed(10), 4)
    check_eq(bits_needed(16), 4)
    check_eq(bits_needed(17), 5)
    check_eq(bits_needed(300), 9)
    check_eq(bits_needed(1_000_000), 20)
